question: A, B and C started a business investing ₹2,410, ₹1,170 and ₹700, respectively. If B's share in the profit earned by them is ₹1,092. what is the difference in the profit (in ₹) earned by A and C?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio of A, B and C = 2410 : 1170 : 700 = 241 : 117 : 70

Difference in profit parts of A and C = 241 − 70 = 171 parts

Profit of B = 117 parts = ₹1,092

Difference in profit = (1092 ÷ 117) × 171 = (28 ÷ 3) × 171 = 28 × 57 = ₹1,596

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,596.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of A = ₹2,410

Investment of B = ₹1,170

Investment of C = ₹700

B's share in the profit = ₹1,092

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Ratio of Product of Capital and Time

When the time period is identical for all partners, Profit Ratio = Ratio of Investment.
